# Sirach Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_012_page_001.jpg

---

**12:1** If you do good, know to whom you do it, and there will be thanks for your good deeds.

**12:2** Do good to the devout, and you will find a reward — if not from him, then from the Most High.

**12:3** No good will come to the one who persists in doing evil, or to the one who does not give alms.

**12:4** Give to the devout, but do not help the sinner. Do good to the humble, but do not give to the ungodly; withhold his bread, and do not give it to him, lest by means of it he overpower you.

**12:5** For you will receive twice as much evil for all the good you may do for him.

**12:6** For the Most High also hates sinners, and will repay vengeance on the ungodly.

**12:7** Give to the good, but do not help the sinner.

**12:8** A friend is not known in prosperity, nor is an enemy hidden in adversity.

**12:9** In a man's prosperity, his enemies are grieved; but in his adversity, even his friend becomes separated from him.

**12:10** Never trust your enemy, for like bronze he rusts, so is his wickedness.

**12:11** Even if he humbles himself and walks stooped, make your soul alert and be on guard against him; and you will be to him like one who has polished a mirror, and you will know that it did not wholly corrode.

**12:12** Do not stand him beside you, lest he overthrow you and stand in your place. Do not seat him at your right hand, lest he seek your seat, and at the last you understand my words and be stung by them.

**12:13** Who will pity a snake charmer who is bitten, or any who come near wild animals?

**12:14** So too, one who associates with a sinful man and is stained by his sins.

**12:15** For a while he will abide with you, but if you stumble, he will not stand firm.

**12:16** An enemy speaks sweetly with his lips, but in his heart he plans to throw you into a pit. The enemy weeps with his eyes, but if he finds opportunity, he will not have enough of your blood.

**12:17** If calamity befalls you, you will find him there before you, and pretending to help, he will undermine your foot.

**12:18** He will wag his head and clap his hands, and whisper many things, and change his countenance.
